messages:
acme-sre: We're seeing intermittent 502 / TLS errors when calling Redwood API from our eu-west-1 VPC. Same requests from us-west-2 succeed. Started ~05:30 UTC. We're on Private (VPC peering + TGW).
maria-support: Sorry — can you paste the client error and a curl -v? Also, are you using Route53 resolver endpoints or the AWS default resolver?
acme-sre: Error snippet:
```
2026-03-16T05:31:12Z call_id=abc123 FAIL: ssl: certificate verify failed: certificate is for "us-west-2.internal.redwood", not "eu-west-1.internal.redwood"
```
curl -v to api.internal.redwood ->
```
* Connected to api.internal.redwood (10.2.45.18) port 443
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, Server hello (2)
* SSL: certificate subject: CN=us-west-2.internal.redwood
* SSL: certificate verify result: unable to verify (1)
```
jonathan-sre: @maria-support adding dig +short from two hosts in different AZs in eu-west-1:
host-a (az-a): dig +short api.internal.redwood -> 10.2.45.18
host-b (az-b): dig +short api.internal.redwood -> 10.7.12.9
Note TTLs are 300.
clara-neteng: Two different private IPs is expected for multi-region failover, but the cert CN should include SANs for both. The cert shown is us-west-2 only — odd.
diego-oncall: Could be a stale /etc/hosts or a cached resolver (systemd-resolved/dnsmasq). Also check egress to Route53 resolver (UDP/TCP 53) across peering/TGW — if blocked, caches persist or TCP fallback fails.
acme-sre: We don't touch /etc/hosts. We run a restrictive egress allowlist; only 53 UDP/TCP to AWS resolver IPs allowed. I can share traceroute + tcpdump.
maria-support: Please run from both hosts and paste:
1) dig +trace api.internal.redwood
2) dig +short @169.254.169.253 api.internal.redwood (or your resolver IP)
3) sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -c 50 port 53
4) sudo curl -v --resolve api.internal.redwood:443:10.7.12.9 https://api.internal.redwood/health
Also include sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward and `cat /etc/resolv.conf` or `systemd-resolve --status`.
acme-sre: Outputs:
- dig +trace shows delegation to our resolver endpoints; answers differ per AZ (10.2.45.18 vs 10.7.12.9)
- dig @169.254.169.253 returns 10.2.45.18 on az-a and 10.7.12.9 on az-b
- tcpdump: many queries to 10.0.5.10:53 (Route53 outbound) with occasional timeouts -> retransmits; some responses dropped
- curl --resolve 10.7.12.9 returns TLS cert for us-west-2
Logs show resolver sometimes returns a stale A record pointing at us-west-2. Maybe resolver cache from before a migration.
clara-neteng: Hypotheses:
- Route53 resolver or local cache has stale entries due to TTL + caching across TGW. Packet loss causing UDP truncation -> TCP fallback issues can leave inconsistent caches.
- Or split-horizon: eu-west-1 resolver occasionally forwarding to an upstream that still answers with us-west-2 IPs (old failover).
maria-support: Immediate mitigations:
- Ensure both UDP and TCP 53 egress allowed reliably between your VPCs and Route53 resolver endpoints. UDP truncation without TCP fallback causes inconsistent answers.
- Temporarily lower TTL on the record (if you control it) to 60s and flush caches: `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` or `sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved` and `sudo killall -HUP dnsmasq` if used.
- Ensure backend TLS certs include SANs for regional hostnames or use a wildcard covering both (e.g., *.internal.redwood) to avoid CN mismatches during cross-region failover.
clara-neteng: Also check Route53 Resolver rules/forwarding and inbound/outbound endpoints — confirm eu-west-1 resolver isn't forwarding to a stale resolver in us-west-2.
diego-oncall: Repro steps for diagnostics team:
1) From az-a and az-b, loop `dig +short api.internal.redwood` every 1s for 2 minutes
2) Capture `sudo tcpdump -i any -n port 53` to pcap
3) Controlled change: set record to us-west-2 only for 60s, switch back, observe propagation and cert behavior
We'll capture now and share pcap link.
maria-support: If you confirm UDP/TCP 53 egress and flush caches but issue persists, we'll escalate to infra to audit private records and cert issuance (cross-region SANs). Please also run `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.45.18:443 -servername api.internal.redwood -showcerts` and attach output.
acme-sre: Uploaded pcap + openssl output. Quick note: after restarting systemd-resolved on az-a, curl returned correct certs for ~5 minutes then drifted again.
maria-support: That pattern points to resolver caching/flapping or intermittent packet loss to resolver. Next steps for us:
- I'll open an internal ticket to request a TTL audit and cert SAN check (infra + certs).
- Clara will review Route53 Resolver configs and peering/TGW ACLs for packet drops.
- Diego will coordinate captures and windows for forcing failovers to correlate events.
Assigning: #infra (clara-neteng), #certs (mike-certs), #support (maria-support). Please update once you confirm allowlist includes UDP/TCP 53 and caches flushed.
acme-sre: Will confirm egress rules and flush caches, then report back. Thanks :pray: 
maria-support: keeping thread open. :mag:
